title: 5 Voice Agent Failure Modes You'll Hit in Week One — Venky B, Plivo
talk_summary: A voice-agent vendor walks through five production failure modes (latency, brittle transcription, unstructured data collection, TTS normalization, turn detection) and the mitigations they use at scale. Most content is voice-specific, but the structured-field-collection and normalization-layer patterns generalize to any LLM agent.

takeaways.technique: Field-level unit tests instead of end-to-end agent evals
takeaways.what_they_do: Model each data-collection target as a typed field (phone number, datetime, name) with validation rules, then test each field as a unit test rather than running hundreds of full agent conversations to find one broken field.
takeaways.numbers: accuracy grew from 30% to 95% from a data collection standpoint

takeaways.technique: Typed schema / constrained output instead of open-ended prompting
takeaways.what_they_do: Decide the output shape before asking: constrain the LLM to typed fields with allowed values and validation, rather than hoping prompt tweaks make it follow instructions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: decide your shape before you ask... instead of keeping it open-ended, can you keep it constrained?

takeaways.technique: Normalization layer between model output and downstream consumer
takeaways.what_they_do: Insert a normalization step (strip markdown/emoji, custom dictionaries, transliteration) between LLM output and TTS so downstream stays engine-independent and doesn't rely on the consumer to clean up.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you usually want to have a normalization layer between your LLM and what is fed to a TTS. You don't send your LLM output directly to a TTS

takeaways.technique: Split small conversational model from larger tool-calling model
takeaways.what_they_do: Use a small/cheap model for the conversational part and a larger model only for tool calling to raise tool-call success ratio while keeping cost/latency down.

takeaways.technique: Dynamic keyword boosting scoped to call state
takeaways.what_they_do: Only boost the keywords relevant to the current phase of the interaction rather than dumping all keywords into context, which causes hallucination.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you just pollute your context of the transcription engine with tons of keywords, it'll start hallucinating again
